# Size and power of the amendment 4 coverage design under the publication delay, at spacing h and h + 1 (#1528)

**Hypothesis and step:** H5, step M5 (registration). **Development data, not a verdict.** Generated by `scripts/coverage_test_delay_power_1528.py page` from `docs/research/coverage-test-delay-power-1528/result.json`, not edited by hand. This is a check on the test: forecasts, the candidate, the protocol and the spacing rule are unchanged, and nothing is registered or published. It feeds #1527 (the spacing amendment). Her ruling of 9 November 2026 (docket "both", then the narrowing on #1528): simulate correct forecasts with the same delay, calendar effects and volatility clustering; measure false rejection and detection power before the spacing rule changes.

## What was measured

The design of amendment 4 (Kupiec and Christoffersen independence at q05/q95 and q01/q99, leads 1 to 5, each regime, Holm over the 200 tests at 5%) was applied to 1000 simulated paths over the real development calendar: 1855 decision days, targets to 2025-12-31, the regimes (2018-19 362, 2020 251, 2021-23 748, 2024 250, 2025-26 244 days) and the class of every target day as the real report has them. A decision on day D reads the last published spread, that of D - 1, so lead h looks h + 1 days ahead of its last value (the one-day publication delay). The data are a latent AR(1) with a two-state Markov volatility (clustering) and a scale by calendar class (quarter-end, month-end, tax date, settlement, policy day), fitted to the development spreads and declared in `metadata/coverage_test_delay_power_1528.json` before any rate was computed: phi 0.643; innovation scale 0.74 calm and 6.40 stress, staying 0.957 and 0.896; class scales month_end 1.51, policy 1.25, quarter_end 4.22, settlement 1.29, tax_date 3.29 (ordinary 1). The true forecaster knows the latent value and the volatility state at D - 1 and the class of its target day, and its distribution is the exact mixture over the volatility paths it cannot see. Three rules are read on the same paths: **h** (the amendment as set: Kupiec and independence on every h-th decision day), **indep h+1** (independence on every (h+1)-th day, Kupiec as set: her ruling on #1525) and **h+1** (both on every (h+1)-th day).

Why spacing matters here, exactly. With the delay, the forecast made on D + h for target D + 2h has not seen the innovation of D + h, and neither has the forecast of D + h seen it: their PITs share it, so hits h apart are dependent for a correct forecaster. The target of the forecast made on D is public when the forecast of D + h + 1 is made, so hits h + 1 apart are independent whatever the data (a martingale argument; the simulation shows it at finite sample). Volatility clustering and calendar effects do not change that; they change power.

**Already measured, not rerun:** #1156 (AR(1) data, no delay: the design near its size), #1516 (the candidate's own PITs bootstrapped, no delay) and #1525 (a calibrated AR(1) forecaster with the D - 1 lag, one regime, normal errors: independence at spacing h rejects 83% to 100% of paths, at h + 1 4% to 8%; size only). This study adds volatility clustering and calendar effects to the delay, and measures power at h + 1, which none measured.

## Power: how often it rejects a misspecified forecaster

Detection is the family-wise rejection rate (Holm at 5%). Because a rule that over-rejects a correct forecaster also detects more, the size-adjusted rate is beside it: the share of paths whose smallest p-value is at most the 5th percentile of that rule's smallest p-value under the true forecaster (thresholds in `result.json`). Band coverage is the share of the forecaster's own PITs inside [0.05, 0.95] on the target days it is misspecified on, so a correct band reads 90%.

## Read-out

- **Size, rule h (amendment 4 as set: Kupiec and independence at spacing h):** a correct forecaster is rejected in 99.3% [98.6%, 99.7%] of paths, above nominal (independence 99.3%, Kupiec 6.8%).
- **Size, rule indep h+1 (independence at spacing h + 1, Kupiec at h (her ruling on #1525)):** a correct forecaster is rejected in 7.0% [5.6%, 8.8%] of paths, above nominal (independence 0.3%, Kupiec 6.7%).
- **Size, rule h+1 (Kupiec and independence both at spacing h + 1):** a correct forecaster is rejected in 1.1% [0.6%, 2.0%] of paths, below nominal (independence 0.3%, Kupiec 0.8%).

- **Detection, rule h** (Holm, size-adjusted in brackets): a_qe75 100% (4%), a_qe50 99% (4%), a_cal75 100% (11%), b_85 100% (11%), b_70 100% (75%), c_lag5 100% (98%), c_lag20 100% (100%).
- **Detection, rule indep h+1** (Holm, size-adjusted in brackets): a_qe75 7% (5%), a_qe50 7% (5%), a_cal75 96% (96%), b_85 63% (60%), b_70 100% (100%), c_lag5 94% (92%), c_lag20 100% (100%).
- **Detection, rule h+1** (Holm, size-adjusted in brackets): a_qe75 1% (5%), a_qe50 2% (6%), a_cal75 63% (77%), b_85 25% (40%), b_70 99% (100%), c_lag5 72% (88%), c_lag20 99% (100%).

- **Fault (a), rule h**, size-adjusted: a_qe75 4%, a_qe50 4%, a_cal75 11%; not detected in all variants (at least 80%).
- **Fault (a), rule indep h+1**, size-adjusted: a_qe75 5%, a_qe50 5%, a_cal75 96%; not detected in all variants (at least 80%).
- **Fault (a), rule h+1**, size-adjusted: a_qe75 5%, a_qe50 6%, a_cal75 77%; not detected in all variants (at least 80%).

**Plainly.**

- Spacing h + 1, rule indep h+1: size is above nominal at 7.0%; the excess is Kupiec's at spacing h (6.7%), independence adds 0.3%. It detects (a) restricted to calendar-class days at 96%, and (a) restricted to quarter-end days at 5% and 5%; narrow overall at 60% and 100%; a stale volatility state at 92% and 100%.
- Spacing h + 1, rule h+1: size is kept (1.1%, not above 5%). It detects (a) restricted to calendar-class days at 77%, and (a) restricted to quarter-end days at 5% and 6%; narrow overall at 40% and 100%; a stale volatility state at 88% and 100%.
- Spacing h (the amendment as set) rejects a correct forecaster in 99% of paths, so its detection of any fault is not informative; size-adjusted, its power against (a) restricted to quarter-end days is 4% and 4%.
- **No spacing both keeps size and detects every variant of (a).** Independence at spacing h + 1 with Kupiec at h is above nominal because of Kupiec at spacing h; both at h + 1 keep size, below nominal, and detect (a) on calendar-class days at less than the other. A fault confined to quarter-end days is not detected at any spacing, the current one included: the report holds too few such days (see the class counts). Detection of an overall narrowing and of a stale volatility state is in the rows above. The rule is not tuned here; #1527 and her own ruling decide.

## What this does and does not show

- It is a simulation of a model fitted to the development spreads, not the candidate: the volatility state is taken as public (a stand-in for the volatility information a real forecaster has), the level and the class means are removed by a correct forecaster and do not enter, and there are two volatility states. A real forecaster's errors are not this model's.
- The misspecified forecasters are the three of the directive (band too narrow on calendar days, narrow overall, a stale volatility state); the narrowing factors and lags are the declaration's, none tuned after a score.
- Quarter-end target days are few in the report (see the class counts above), so power against a quarter-end-only fault is limited by how many such days a regime holds, at any spacing; #1531 is the arm that studies that day type.
- It changes no rule and registers nothing. Whether to read independence at spacing h + 1 is hers (#1527); this page says what the rule would give.
- Development data, not a verdict: no locked day, nothing after 2025-12-31.
